words.enDefinition: a casual collarless top usually with short sleeves

examples.en: I wore a T-shirt to the club picnic because the afternoon was still warm.
examples.zh: 下午还挺暖和，我穿着「T恤」去参加了社团野餐。

examples.en: The T-shirt from last year's campus run is still my favorite thing to sleep in.
examples.zh: 去年校园跑活动发的「T恤」还是我最喜欢穿着睡觉的衣服。

words.enDefinition: a casual top with a collar and short button opening

examples.en: We each wore a polo shirt and dark trousers during our shifts at the registration desk.
examples.zh: 我们去登记台值班时穿「翻领短袖衫」和深色长裤。

examples.en: I packed a polo shirt for the student society dinner after the afternoon game.
examples.zh: 我在包里放了件「翻领短袖衫」，准备下午比赛后去参加社团聚餐。

words.enDefinition: a shirt with buttons that hold down its collar points

examples.en: I wore a button-down shirt to my presentation because the collar stays flat under a sweater.
examples.zh: 做汇报时我穿了件「领尖带扣的衬衫」，因为套上毛衣后领子也能保持平整。

examples.en: The button-down shirt looked neat even after I took off my jacket in the library.
examples.zh: 在图书馆脱下夹克后，那件「领尖带扣的衬衫」看起来还是很整齐。

words.enDefinition: a sleeveless top with straps over the shoulders

examples.en: I wore a tank top under my shirt because the lecture hall gets warm.
examples.zh: 我在衬衫里穿了件「无袖背心」，因为阶梯教室里会变热。

examples.en: She changed into a tank top before joining the group for badminton in the garden.
examples.zh: 加入大家在花园打羽毛球前，她换上了一件「无袖背心」。

collocations: layer a jacket over a tank top

words.enDefinition: a warm casual pullover made from thick soft fabric

examples.en: I grabbed a sweatshirt on my way out because the library gets chilly after dark.
examples.zh: 我出门时随手拿了件「卫衣」，图书馆天黑后有点冷。

examples.en: My roommate recognized the sweatshirt from the small logo on its left sleeve.
examples.zh: 室友从左袖上的小标志认出了那件「卫衣」。

words.enDefinition: a casual sweatshirt or jacket with an attached hood

examples.en: I wore my hoodie under a coat so I could pull the hood up outside.
examples.zh: 我在大衣下面穿了「连帽卫衣」，这样到外面就能把帽子拉起来。

examples.en: I left my hoodie on the back of a chair after our evening study group.
examples.zh: 晚上的学习小组结束后，我把「连帽卫衣」忘在椅背上了。

words.enDefinition: a knitted top worn for warmth, often pulled over the head

examples.en: I keep a sweater in my locker for afternoons when the seminar room gets cold.
examples.zh: 下午研讨课教室有时很冷，所以我在储物柜里放了件「毛衣」。

examples.en: The sweater was warm enough for our walk back across campus after the film.
examples.zh: 电影散场后，这件「毛衣」够暖，穿着走回校园另一头也不冷。

words.enDefinition: a knitted garment that opens down the front

examples.en: I left my cardigan open because the study room warmed up when more people arrived.
examples.zh: 人多起来后，自习室暖和了，我就敞着「开襟毛衣」。

examples.en: She kept a cardigan over her chair so she could grab it after class.
examples.zh: 她把「开襟毛衣」搭在椅背上，下课就能拿走。

words.enDefinition: a lightweight jacket designed to keep the wind out

examples.en: I took a windbreaker for the walk across the bridge because it gets windy there.
examples.zh: 过桥那段路风大，我带了件「防风夹克」。

examples.en: The windbreaker folds small enough to fit beside my lunch box in my bag.
examples.zh: 「防风夹克」折起来挺小，能在包里塞到饭盒旁边。

words.enDefinition: a warm jacket with filling in puffed sections

examples.en: I waited for the bus in my puffer jacket while frost formed on the benches.
examples.zh: 长椅上慢慢结了霜，我穿着「蓬松绗缝保暖外套」等公交。

examples.en: The puffer jacket took up most of the space on my tiny coat hook.
examples.zh: 我那小小的衣钩几乎都被「蓬松绗缝保暖外套」占满了。

words.enDefinition: a jacket made from sturdy denim fabric

examples.en: I wore a denim jacket to the film club meeting because we sat outside.
examples.zh: 电影社开会坐在室外，我就穿了一件「牛仔夹克」。

examples.en: The denim jacket was just warm enough for the walk from residence to the station.
examples.zh: 从宿舍走到车站，穿那件「牛仔夹克」刚好够暖。

collocations: layer a denim jacket over a sweater

words.enDefinition: a soft warm jacket made of fleece fabric

examples.en: The fleece jacket kept me warm in the studio while the windows were open.
examples.zh: 工作室开着窗，我穿「抓绒外套」也不觉得冷。

examples.en: I left a fleece jacket in my gym locker for the walk home afterwards.
examples.zh: 我在健身房的储物柜里放了件「抓绒外套」，以便结束后走回家时穿。

words.enDefinition: a sleeveless outer garment worn over another layer for warmth

examples.en: At my university in England, I wore a gilet when biking to early lectures.
examples.zh: 在英格兰上大学时，我骑车去上早课会穿「无袖保暖外套」。

examples.en: I put a gilet over my sweater because I wanted my arms free for carrying boxes.
examples.zh: 我在毛衣外套了件「无袖保暖外套」，方便活动手臂搬箱子。

words.enDefinition: casual trousers that narrow and usually fit closely at the ankles

examples.en: I wore joggers to the volunteer cleanup because the cuffs would stay above my shoes.
examples.zh: 我穿「束脚休闲裤」参加了志愿清理活动，因为裤脚不会拖到鞋上。

examples.en: My roommate packs joggers for the train because they're comfortable for a long trip.
examples.zh: 室友坐火车时会带「束脚休闲裤」，长途穿着舒服。

words.enDefinition: soft casual trousers made of thick sweatshirt material

examples.en: I stayed in sweatpants all morning while I worked on the presentation in my room.
examples.zh: 我一上午都穿着「厚软运动裤」在房间里做演示稿。

examples.en: The sweatpants were warm enough for sitting outside after our early morning sports session.
examples.zh: 清早的运动课结束后，在外面坐着穿「厚软运动裤」也够暖。

words.enDefinition: stretchy close-fitting trousers worn for exercise or casual use

examples.en: I changed into leggings for the campus yoga class before meeting friends for lunch.
examples.zh: 去和朋友吃午饭前，我换上「紧身弹力裤」去上学校的瑜伽课。

examples.en: She wore leggings under a long sweater on the day we toured the museum.
examples.zh: 参观博物馆那天，她在长毛衣下面穿了「紧身弹力裤」。

words.enDefinition: tights made from fabric that you cannot see through

examples.en: I wore opaque tights under my skirt because we were walking back late at night.
examples.zh: 我们要深夜走回去，所以我在裙子下面穿了「不透肤连裤袜」。

examples.en: She packed opaque tights for the student concert to go with her dark dress.
examples.zh: 她带了「不透肤连裤袜」去学生音乐会，搭配自己的深色连衣裙。

words.enDefinition: casual trousers made from smooth cotton twill fabric

examples.en: I wore chinos to the campus tour because I wanted something comfortable but tidy.
examples.zh: 我穿着「斜纹棉布休闲裤」带人参观校园，想穿得既舒服又整齐。

examples.en: The chinos went with the sweater I'd brought for dinner with my project group.
examples.zh: 这条「斜纹棉布休闲裤」和我给项目组聚餐带的毛衣很搭。

words.enDefinition: trousers with large pockets, especially on the sides of the legs

examples.en: I wore cargo pants for the workshop because I could keep my tape measure handy.
examples.zh: 我穿「工装裤」去工坊，能把卷尺放在随手拿得到的地方。

examples.en: My cargo pants have a side pocket that fits my bus pass and keys.
examples.zh: 我的「工装裤」有个侧袋，可以放公交卡和钥匙。

words.enDefinition: the layer of clothing worn closest to the skin

examples.en: I wore a base layer under my sweater for the early morning field trip.
examples.zh: 一大早去实地考察，我在毛衣下面穿了件「贴身打底层」。

examples.en: The base layer was useful when I had to wait outside for the first bus.
examples.zh: 要在外面等头班公交时，「贴身打底层」派上了用场。

words.enDefinition: a heavy shirt worn over another top like a jacket

examples.en: I wore an overshirt over my T-shirt because the lecture hall is usually cool.
examples.zh: 阶梯教室通常有点凉，我就在T恤外加了件「外搭衬衫」。

examples.en: The overshirt was easy to take off when our group moved into the warm studio.
examples.zh: 我们小组进了暖和的工作室后，那件「外搭衬衫」很容易脱下来。

words.enDefinition: neat trousers meant for formal or professional occasions

examples.en: I saved my dress pants for the reception where we were meeting our project sponsors.
examples.zh: 我把「正装长裤」留到招待会穿，那时要见项目资助方。

examples.en: The dress pants looked fine with the only plain shirt I had in my room.
examples.zh: 这条「正装长裤」搭我房间里唯一那件素色衬衫就挺合适。

collocations: pair dress pants with a shirt

words.enDefinition: a tailored jacket designed to be worn without matching trousers

examples.en: I wore a blazer over a plain T-shirt for the final project presentation on campus.
examples.zh: 在学校做最终项目汇报时，我在素色T恤外穿了件「休闲西装外套」。

examples.en: The navy blazer worked with the trousers I'd already brought from home for the event.
examples.zh: 这件藏青色的「休闲西装外套」和我从家里带来出席活动的裤子挺搭。

words.enDefinition: a sleeveless garment typically worn over a shirt and under a suit jacket

examples.en: My cousin wore a waistcoat for the college concert and took his jacket off backstage.
examples.zh: 我表弟穿着「西装马甲」参加学院音乐会，在后台脱了外套。

examples.en: I borrowed a waistcoat from a friend for our student theatre production last term.
examples.zh: 上学期学生剧团演出时，我跟朋友借了一件「西装马甲」。

words.enDefinition: the jacket made to match the other pieces of a suit

examples.en: I kept the suit jacket with its matching trousers until the morning of my presentation.
examples.zh: 汇报当天早上之前，我一直把「套装中的西装上衣」和配套西裤放在一起。

examples.en: My suit jacket was over the back of my chair after the award ceremony.
examples.zh: 颁奖典礼结束后，我的「套装中的西装上衣」搭在椅背上。

words.enDefinition: a loose robe worn after bathing or while getting dressed

examples.en: I keep a bathrobe by the door for walking back from the shared shower.
examples.zh: 我在门边放了件「浴袍」，方便洗完澡从共用淋浴间走回来。

examples.en: My bathrobe was still over the chair when my flatmate knocked to borrow a towel.
examples.zh: 室友敲门来借毛巾时，我的「浴袍」还搭在椅子上。

words.enDefinition: a light sleeveless top with thin shoulder straps

examples.en: I wore a camisole under my open shirt on the walk across campus in July.
examples.zh: 七月走过校园时，我在敞开的衬衫里穿了件「细肩带上衣」。

examples.en: The camisole stayed comfortable under my sweater while I worked in the heated studio.
examples.zh: 我在有暖气的工作室做事时，毛衣下面穿「细肩带上衣」也挺舒服。

collocations: layer a camisole under a shirt

words.enDefinition: a shirt with sleeves extending to the wrists

examples.en: I wore a long-sleeved shirt because the study room was chilly in the morning.
examples.zh: 早上自习室有点凉，所以我穿了件「长袖衬衫」。

examples.en: I packed a long-sleeved shirt for the evening meal after our trip to the coast.
examples.zh: 我带了件「长袖衬衫」，准备从海边回来后吃晚饭时穿。

words.enDefinition: a top with a tall collar that folds around the neck

examples.en: My turtleneck kept my neck warm on the walk to the library after sunset.
examples.zh: 太阳下山后走去图书馆的路上，我的「高领上衣」把脖子裹得挺暖。

examples.en: I wore a turtleneck under the blazer for our presentation in the cold lecture hall.
examples.zh: 我们在冷飕飕的阶梯教室做汇报，我在西装外套下面穿了「高领上衣」。

words.enDefinition: trousers with a front bib held up by shoulder straps

examples.en: At my UK university, I wore dungarees to the community garden cleanup last Saturday.
examples.zh: 上周六，我在英国的大学参加社区花园清理活动时，穿了「背带连体裤」。

examples.en: Her dungarees were useful in the art studio because they had several deep pockets.
examples.zh: 她的「背带连体裤」有几个很深的口袋，在美术工作室穿挺方便。

words.enDefinition: a loose waterproof covering worn over the shoulders and body

examples.en: I packed a rain poncho because the campus concert was going ahead outdoors.
examples.zh: 校园音乐会照常在室外举行，我就带了件「雨披」。

examples.en: The rain poncho covered my backpack when I walked from the station to residence.
examples.zh: 我从车站走回宿舍时，「雨披」把背包也罩住了。

words.enDefinition: short trousers worn for swimming

examples.en: I packed swim trunks and a towel for the residence trip to the pool.
examples.zh: 宿舍集体去游泳池，我带上了「泳裤」和毛巾。

examples.en: My swim trunks were still damp when I got back from the campus pool.
examples.zh: 从学校游泳池回来时，我的「泳裤」还是潮的。

words.enDefinition: the shape of the opening for the neck in a garment

examples.en: I chose the top with a higher neckline because I would be outside all evening.
examples.zh: 我要在外面待一整晚，所以选了那件「领口较高」的上衣。

examples.en: The neckline of my sweater sat neatly above the collar of the jacket.
examples.zh: 我的毛衣「领口」正好整齐地露在夹克领子上方。

words.enDefinition: a round neckline that sits close to the base of the neck

examples.en: I chose a sweater with a crew neck for the walk home after class.
examples.zh: 我选了件「贴颈圆领」毛衣，下课后走回家时穿。

examples.en: The sweatshirt had a crew neck that sat flat under my raincoat all afternoon.
examples.zh: 卫衣是「贴颈圆领」，一下午都平贴在雨衣下面。

collocations: a crew neck on a sweater

words.enDefinition: a neckline shaped like the letter V

examples.en: The sweater has a V-neck, so the collar of my shirt stays visible.
examples.zh: 毛衣是「V形领口」，我的衬衫领还能露出来。

examples.en: I preferred the V-neck on the blue sweater with the scarf I already owned.
examples.zh: 搭我原来的围巾时，我更喜欢蓝毛衣的「V形领口」。

words.enDefinition: the part of a garment that fits around the neck

examples.en: I turned up my collar when the wind picked up outside the student centre.
examples.zh: 学生中心外起风了，我就把「衣领」竖起来。

examples.en: She straightened the collar of her shirt before we took the group photo.
examples.zh: 拍合影前，她理了理衬衫的「衣领」。

words.enDefinition: the finished band at the end of a sleeve

examples.en: One cuff kept catching on the edge of my notebook during the lecture.
examples.zh: 上课时，一个「袖口」老是勾到笔记本的边。

examples.en: I loosened the cuff of my shirt before washing my hands in the studio.
examples.zh: 在工作室洗手前，我把衬衫的「袖口」松开了。

words.enDefinition: the finished lower edge of a piece of clothing

examples.en: The hem of my skirt got wet on the walk home through the garden.
examples.zh: 穿过花园走回家时，我的裙子「下摆」湿了。

examples.en: I folded the hem of the costume under so it wouldn't drag on stage.
examples.zh: 我把演出服的「下摆」折进去，免得在舞台上拖地。

words.enDefinition: the strip of material around the waist of trousers or a skirt

examples.en: I sat for most of the train journey, and the elastic waistband felt comfortable.
examples.zh: 火车上大部分时间我都坐着，裤子有「松紧腰头」，穿着挺舒服。

examples.en: The loose end of the drawstring disappeared into the waistband during our practice.
examples.zh: 练习时，抽绳松开的那一头缩进了「裤腰」里。

words.enDefinition: a small loop on trousers that holds a belt in place

examples.en: I clipped my keys to a belt loop before walking over to the workshop.
examples.zh: 我出发去工坊前，把钥匙扣在一个「裤袢」上。

examples.en: The last belt loop had a loose thread that caught on the door handle.
examples.zh: 最后一个「裤袢」有根松线，勾到了门把手上。

collocations: thread a belt through a belt loop

words.enDefinition: a cord pulled through an opening to tighten it

examples.en: I tightened the drawstring on my hood before cycling across the open courtyard.
examples.zh: 骑车穿过空旷的院子前，我把帽子上的「抽绳」拉紧了。

examples.en: The drawstring in my trousers worked its way loose on the way to class.
examples.zh: 去上课的路上，我裤子里的「抽绳」慢慢松开了。

words.enDefinition: the small tab you hold to move a zipper

examples.en: The zipper pull on my jacket was hard to grip with my mittens on.
examples.zh: 戴着连指手套时，我很难捏住夹克的「拉链拉片」。

examples.en: I tied a short ribbon to the zipper pull so I could find it easily.
examples.zh: 我在「拉链拉片」上系了根短丝带，这样就容易找到它了。

words.enDefinition: a pocket that closes with a zipper

examples.en: I put my bike key in a zip pocket before setting out for the library.
examples.zh: 出发去图书馆前，我把自行车钥匙放进了「拉链口袋」。

examples.en: The zip pocket was the only part of my jacket where the coins stayed put.
examples.zh: 我这件夹克只有「拉链口袋」能让硬币好好待在里面。

collocations: keep keys in a zip pocket

words.enDefinition: a pocket on the inner side of a garment

examples.en: I kept the concert tickets in an inside pocket so the rain couldn't reach them.
examples.zh: 我把音乐会门票放在「内侧口袋」里，这样就不会被雨淋到。

examples.en: My jacket has an inside pocket that fits the small timetable I printed this morning.
examples.zh: 我的夹克有个「内侧口袋」，正好放得下早上打印的小时间表。

collocations: keep something in an inside pocket

words.enDefinition: a pocket high on the front of a shirt or jacket

examples.en: I kept a pen in my chest pocket while checking people in at the event.
examples.zh: 给参加活动的人签到时，我把一支笔放在「胸前口袋」里。

examples.en: The chest pocket on my overshirt was just big enough for my student card.
examples.zh: 我外搭衬衫的「胸前口袋」刚好能装下学生证。

collocations: keep a pen in a chest pocket

words.enDefinition: a head covering attached to a coat or top

examples.en: I pulled my hood up as soon as I stepped outside the library.
examples.zh: 我一走出图书馆就把「兜帽」拉起来。

examples.en: The hood of my jacket kept brushing against the back of the bus seat.
examples.zh: 我夹克的「兜帽」总蹭到公交车的椅背。

words.enDefinition: one of the folded flaps below a jacket collar

examples.en: The club gave me a small pin to wear on my lapel at the reception.
examples.zh: 社团给了我一枚小徽章，让我在招待会上别在「西装翻领」上。

examples.en: I noticed one lapel sat higher than the other in our student theatre costume.
examples.zh: 我发现学生剧团那套戏服的一边「西装翻领」比另一边高。

words.enDefinition: made without sleeves

examples.en: I wore a sleeveless top indoors and put a cardigan over it outside.
examples.zh: 在室内我穿「无袖的」上衣，到外面就套一件开襟毛衣。

examples.en: The costume is sleeveless, so I brought a sweater for the break between rehearsals.
examples.zh: 戏服是「无袖的」，我带了件毛衣，排练间歇可以穿。

words.enDefinition: socks that end around the ankle

examples.en: I packed ankle socks for the gym because they sit just above my shoes.
examples.zh: 我去健身房带了「踝袜」，袜口刚好比鞋口高一点。

examples.en: My ankle socks got wet when I stepped in a puddle outside the hall.
examples.zh: 我在大厅外踩进水坑，「踝袜」湿了。

words.enDefinition: low socks designed to stay hidden inside shoes

examples.en: I wore no-show socks with my loafers for the student society dinner last night.
examples.zh: 昨晚我穿乐福鞋去参加社团聚餐，搭的是「隐形袜」。

examples.en: My no-show socks stayed hidden even when I sat down with my ankles crossed.
examples.zh: 我坐下交叉脚踝时，「隐形袜」也没有露出来。

words.enDefinition: socks that cover the ankle and reach partway up the calf

examples.en: I wore crew socks with my boots so the tops didn't rub against my legs.
examples.zh: 我穿靴子时搭了「中筒袜」，这样靴口就不会直接蹭腿。

examples.en: She packed crew socks for the weekend trip because the evenings were still cold.
examples.zh: 那几天晚上还冷，她给周末出行带上了「中筒袜」。

words.enDefinition: a cord threaded through a shoe to fasten it

examples.en: I tucked a loose shoelace into my shoe before going down the dorm stairs.
examples.zh: 下宿舍楼梯前，我把一根松掉的「鞋带」塞进鞋里。

examples.en: One shoelace broke just as I was getting ready to leave for class.
examples.zh: 我刚准备出门上课，一根「鞋带」就断了。

words.enDefinition: the layer inside a shoe on which the foot rests

examples.en: The insole came loose when I took off my shoes after the campus walk.
examples.zh: 绕校园走完后我脱下鞋，发现「鞋内垫」松了。

examples.en: I put the insole back into my shoe after it slipped out in the hallway.
examples.zh: 「鞋内垫」掉在走廊里，我捡起来放回了鞋里。

words.enDefinition: the bottom part of a shoe that touches the ground

examples.en: A pebble got wedged in my shoe sole during our walk along the river.
examples.zh: 我们沿河散步时，一颗小石子卡在了我的「鞋底」上。

examples.en: I noticed mud on my shoe sole before stepping into the study room.
examples.zh: 走进自习室前，我发现「鞋底」上有泥。

words.enDefinition: casual shoes with flexible soles often worn for exercise

examples.en: I wore sneakers because the campus tour involved walking between several buildings before lunch.
examples.zh: 我穿了「运动休闲鞋」，因为午饭前参观校园要在几栋楼之间走动。

examples.en: My sneakers were still damp from rain, so I left them by the door.
examples.zh: 我的「运动休闲鞋」淋了雨还没干，我把它们留在门边。

words.enDefinition: boots that rise as high as the ankle

examples.en: I wore ankle boots on the walk home when the paths were covered in leaves.
examples.zh: 小路上铺满落叶，我穿着「及踝短靴」走回家。

examples.en: She changed out of her ankle boots after the student theatre rehearsal ended.
examples.zh: 学生剧团排练结束后，她换下了「及踝短靴」。

words.enDefinition: low slip-on shoes with a flat heel, often made of leather

examples.en: I wore loafers to the awards ceremony because the hall was next to my residence.
examples.zh: 颁奖典礼的礼堂就在宿舍旁边，所以我穿了「乐福鞋」。

examples.en: My loafers looked neat with dress pants at the end-of-term dinner on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五的期末聚餐上，我的「乐福鞋」配正装长裤看起来挺整齐。

words.enDefinition: shoes you put on without tying laces or doing up fasteners

examples.en: I keep slip-ons by the door for quick trips to the laundry room downstairs.
examples.zh: 我在门边放了双「一脚蹬便鞋」，方便临时去楼下洗衣房。

examples.en: The slip-ons were handy when we had to leave our shoes outside the studio.
examples.zh: 我们得把鞋留在工作室外面时，「一脚蹬便鞋」穿脱起来很方便。

words.enDefinition: open shoes held on the foot by straps

examples.en: I wore sandals to the outdoor film because the evening was still warm.
examples.zh: 晚上依旧暖和，所以我穿着「凉鞋」去看露天电影。

examples.en: My sandals fit easily into the side of my bag beside my towel.
examples.zh: 我的「凉鞋」很容易塞进包的一侧，放在毛巾旁边。

words.enDefinition: two padded covers worn over the ears to keep them warm

examples.en: I put on earmuffs for the walk to the bus stop before sunrise.
examples.zh: 天亮前走去公交站时，我戴了「保暖耳罩」。

examples.en: She took off her earmuffs as soon as we entered the heated library.
examples.zh: 我们一进有暖气的图书馆，她就摘了「保暖耳罩」。

words.enDefinition: hand coverings with one section for the fingers and another for the thumb

examples.en: I tucked my mittens into my coat pockets before going into the café.
examples.zh: 进咖啡馆前，我把「连指手套」塞进大衣口袋。

examples.en: I had to take off my mittens to scan the student card at the door.
examples.zh: 为了在门口刷学生证，我得先脱掉「连指手套」。

words.enDefinition: a soft hat with a stiff bill at the front

examples.en: I wore a baseball cap to the rowing event because there was no shade.
examples.zh: 赛艇活动那里没遮阳的地方，我戴着「棒球帽」去了。

examples.en: The baseball cap from the student club had a small logo on the side.
examples.zh: 学生社团发的「棒球帽」侧面有个小标志。

words.enDefinition: the fastener that joins the ends of a belt

examples.en: My belt buckle caught the light when we walked back from the student theatre.
examples.zh: 我们从学生剧院走回来时，我的「皮带扣」在灯光下一闪。

examples.en: I checked that the belt buckle was centered before we took our group photo.
examples.zh: 拍合影前，我确认「皮带扣」对在正中间。

words.enDefinition: put on clothes or shoes in one easy motion

examples.en: I can slip on my shoes here before we head out to the courtyard.
examples.zh: 我们去院子之前，我可以在这儿「轻松套上」鞋。

examples.en: I'll slip on a cardigan before going downstairs to meet the rest of the group.
examples.zh: 我先「套上」一件开襟毛衣，再下楼去和其他人碰面。

collocations: slip on a pair of sandals

words.enDefinition: take off your shoes with a quick movement of your feet

examples.en: You can kick off your shoes by the door before coming into the room.
examples.zh: 进房间前，你可以在门边「蹬掉鞋子」。

examples.en: It's nice to kick off your shoes after walking across campus all afternoon.
examples.zh: 下午在校园里走来走去，回来「蹬掉鞋子」真舒服。

collocations: kick off your shoes by the door
kick off your shoes and relax
kick off your shoes after class

words.enDefinition: a line where two pieces of fabric are joined

examples.en: I found a loose thread along the side seam of my jacket after rehearsal.
examples.zh: 排练过后，我发现夹克侧面的「接缝」上有个松了的线头。

examples.en: The seam on the inside of my sleeve caught on the corner of the shelf.
examples.zh: 袖子里面的「接缝」被架子的尖角勾住了。

words.enDefinition: put the bottom of your shirt inside your trousers or skirt

examples.en: Could you tuck in your shirt before we take the photo for the society newsletter?
examples.zh: 拍社团通讯用的照片前，你能「把衬衫塞进裤腰」吗？

examples.en: It's easier to tuck in your shirt if you take off the jacket first.
examples.zh: 可以先把外套脱下来，这样更容易「把衬衫塞进裤腰」。

collocations: tuck in your shirt before a photo
remember to tuck in your shirt

words.enDefinition: fold your sleeves upwards so they sit higher on your arms

examples.en: You might want to roll up your sleeves before washing the paintbrushes in the studio.
examples.zh: 在工作室洗画笔前，你可以先「把袖子卷起来」。

examples.en: I remember the tutor saying to roll up your sleeves before mixing the clay.
examples.zh: 我记得导师说过，和黏土前要「把袖子卷起来」。

collocations: roll up your sleeves before washing
roll up your sleeves to the elbows
remember to roll up your sleeves

words.enDefinition: unfasten one button on a piece of clothing

examples.en: I stopped to undo a button because the seminar room was getting quite warm.
examples.zh: 研讨课教室越来越暖和，我停下来「解开了一颗扣子」。

examples.en: I had to undo a button before I could get the shirt over my head.
examples.zh: 我得先「解开一颗扣子」，才能把衬衫从头上套过去。

collocations: undo a button on your collar
undo a button at the cuff

words.enDefinition: open something by sliding its zipper down or across

examples.en: You can unzip your jacket once we get inside the warm lecture hall.
examples.zh: 我们进了暖和的阶梯教室，你就可以「拉开夹克的拉链」。

examples.en: I had to unzip the pocket to find my key at the residence entrance.
examples.zh: 到了宿舍入口，我得「拉开口袋的拉链」找钥匙。

words.enDefinition: fasten the ends of a belt with its buckle

examples.en: Make sure to buckle your belt before we start taking photos for the play.
examples.zh: 我们开始给剧目拍照前，记得「扣好皮带」。

examples.en: It's easier to buckle your belt before you put the long jacket on.
examples.zh: 穿上长外套之前，「扣好皮带」更方便。

words.enDefinition: become loose or undone after being tied

examples.en: My shoelaces tend to come untied when I walk quickly between classes.
examples.zh: 赶着在教室之间走时，我的鞋带经常「自己松开」。

examples.en: The drawstring can come untied if I leave the ends hanging outside my coat.
examples.zh: 如果把抽绳的两头留在外套外面，结就可能「自己松开」。

words.enDefinition: turn up the bottoms of your jeans to make them shorter

examples.en: You can cuff your jeans so the loose ends don't drag through the puddles.
examples.zh: 你可以「卷起牛仔裤脚」，这样松松的裤脚就不会拖过水坑。

examples.en: It's easier to cuff your jeans before you lace up those ankle boots.
examples.zh: 给那双短靴系鞋带之前，「卷起牛仔裤脚」会更方便。

collocations: cuff your jeans above your boots
learn how to cuff your jeans

words.enDefinition: with the inner surface facing outward

examples.en: I wore my T-shirt inside out to breakfast and only noticed when someone pointed it out.
examples.zh: 我早餐时把T恤穿得「里子朝外」，有人提醒后才注意到。

examples.en: My sleeve was inside out after I pulled the sweater off in a hurry.
examples.zh: 我匆忙脱掉毛衣，袖子翻成了「里子朝外」。

collocations: check if it is inside out

words.enDefinition: with the back of a garment facing forward

examples.en: I rushed to rehearsal and put my costume on back to front by mistake.
examples.zh: 我赶去排练，不小心把戏服「前后穿反了」。

examples.en: My scarf hid the fact that I'd put the sweater on back to front.
examples.zh: 围巾遮住了，所以看不出来我的毛衣「前后穿反了」。

collocations: wear a top back to front
put a shirt on back to front

words.enDefinition: put on several layers of clothes for warmth

examples.en: We decided to layer up for the outdoor concert because it would cool down after sunset.
examples.zh: 户外音乐会在太阳落山后会变凉，我们决定「多穿几层」。

examples.en: I had to layer up before leaving the dorm for the early morning bus.
examples.zh: 一大早从宿舍出发去坐公交前，我得「多穿几层」。

words.enDefinition: wear less formal clothes than usual or than expected

examples.en: We can dress down for the practice presentation because it's just our project group.
examples.zh: 练习汇报只有项目组自己人，我们可以「穿得随意些」。

examples.en: I decided to dress down for the picnic and left my blazer at home.
examples.zh: 我决定去野餐时「穿得随意些」，就把西装外套留在住处。

collocations: dress down for a casual event

words.enDefinition: put something on quickly without much planning

examples.en: I had time to throw on a jacket before the others left the flat.
examples.zh: 其他人离开公寓前，我来得及「随手穿上」一件夹克。

examples.en: I'll throw on whatever sweater is closest and meet you by the lift.
examples.zh: 我「随手穿上」离我最近的那件毛衣，在电梯旁和你碰面。

words.enDefinition: combine different pieces in a variety of ways

examples.en: I packed three tops I could mix and match with the same trousers.
examples.zh: 我带了三件上衣，能和同一条裤子「混搭」。

examples.en: The costumes let us mix and match pieces from different years of the theatre club.
examples.zh: 戏服可以让我们把剧团不同年份的衣服「混搭」着穿。

collocations: mix and match tops and trousers

words.enDefinition: choose things with colors that look good together

examples.en: We decided to color-coordinate our shirts for the photo on the student magazine cover.
examples.zh: 我们决定给衬衫「协调配色」，拍学生杂志封面照片。

examples.en: I tried to color-coordinate my scarf and sweater before the end-of-term dinner on campus.
examples.zh: 学校的期末聚餐前，我试着给自己的围巾和毛衣「协调配色」。

words.enDefinition: look unattractive together because colors or patterns compete
acceptedZhAnswers: 跟某物搭配起来不协调

examples.en: The bright scarf might clash with my patterned shirt in the theatre group's photo.
examples.zh: 拍剧团合照时，那条亮色围巾可能「和我的花衬衫不搭」。

examples.en: I picked plain trousers so they wouldn't clash with the jacket I'd already chosen.
examples.zh: 我选了素色长裤，这样就不会「和已选好的夹克不搭」。

collocations: clash with the rest of the outfit

words.enDefinition: informal clothes suitable for everyday activities

examples.en: The invitation says casual wear is fine, so I'll wear the same clothes as today.
examples.zh: 邀请函说穿「休闲服装」就行，我就穿今天这一套。

examples.en: I packed mostly casual wear because we were staying in a cabin for the weekend.
examples.zh: 周末我们住小木屋，所以我带的大多是「休闲服装」。

words.enDefinition: neat and comfortable, in a style between casual and formal

examples.en: The student society dinner is smart casual, so I'm wearing a neat shirt and chinos.
examples.zh: 学生社团聚餐要求「穿得体面又不必太正式」，所以我穿整齐的衬衫配休闲裤。

examples.en: I asked what smart casual meant for the reception before I packed my bag.
examples.zh: 收拾行李前，我问招待会要求的「得体而不太正式」具体是怎么穿。

words.enDefinition: neat and informal in a way suited to some workplaces

examples.en: The employer described the campus networking lunch as business casual in the invitation.
examples.zh: 用人单位的邀请函写着，校园交流午餐会穿「商务休闲」服装。

examples.en: I asked whether clean sneakers were acceptable with business casual clothes for the event.
examples.zh: 我问活动穿「商务休闲」服装时，能不能配干净的运动鞋。

words.enDefinition: clothing intended for formal occasions or ceremonies

examples.en: I borrowed formalwear from a friend for the awards ceremony in the main hall.
examples.zh: 我向朋友借了「正式场合服装」，去主礼堂参加颁奖典礼。

examples.en: The invitation asked for formalwear because the student orchestra was performing at a gala.
examples.zh: 邀请函要求穿「正式场合服装」，学生管弦乐团那天要在正式晚会上演出。

words.enDefinition: able to keep out some water during light exposure

examples.en: I wore a water-resistant jacket for the short walk from the library to the café.
examples.zh: 从图书馆走一小段到咖啡馆时，我穿了件「防泼水的」夹克。

examples.en: The water-resistant fabric kept the light drizzle off my trousers during the campus tour.
examples.zh: 参观校园时，「防泼水的」布料挡住了落在长裤上的细雨。

words.enDefinition: letting air or moisture pass through, so you stay comfortable

examples.en: I wore a breathable top for the walk to class because it was warm outside.
examples.zh: 外面挺热，我穿了件「透气的」上衣走去教室。

examples.en: The studio was stuffy, so I was glad my shirt was made from breathable fabric.
examples.zh: 工作室里挺闷，我庆幸自己的衬衫用的是「透气的」布料。

words.enDefinition: becoming dry again in a short time

examples.en: I packed a quick-drying shirt because we were spending the afternoon at the lake.
examples.zh: 下午要在湖边玩，所以我带了件「快干的」衬衫。

examples.en: The quick-drying socks were handy on the field trip after we got caught in rain.
examples.zh: 实地考察时我们遇上了雨，「快干的」袜子派上了用场。

words.enDefinition: made to stay smooth without easily forming creases

examples.en: I packed a wrinkle-resistant shirt for the conference because it had to fit in my backpack.
examples.zh: 出席会议的衣服得塞进背包，所以我带了一件「不易起皱的」衬衫。

examples.en: Her wrinkle-resistant trousers still looked neat after the long train ride back to campus.
examples.zh: 坐了很久火车回学校，她那条「不易起皱的」长裤看起来还是挺整齐。

words.enDefinition: made with an extra layer of material on the inside

examples.en: My lined jacket kept me warm while we waited outside the theatre after rehearsal.
examples.zh: 排练后在剧院外等候时，我那件「加了内衬的」夹克挺暖和。

examples.en: The lined skirt was comfortable to wear while walking across campus in the wind.
examples.zh: 刮风时穿过校园，穿那条「加了内衬的」裙子挺舒服。

words.enDefinition: designed to be worn with either side facing outwards

examples.en: I wore the plain side of my reversible jacket to dinner with my project group.
examples.zh: 跟项目组一起吃晚饭时，我把「两面可穿的」夹克翻到素色那面穿。

examples.en: The reversible vest let us switch team colors halfway through practice on the field.
examples.zh: 「两面可穿的」背心让我们能在球场训练到一半时换队服颜色。

words.enDefinition: a strap whose length can be changed

examples.en: My sandal has an adjustable strap that I loosened after the long walk.
examples.zh: 走了很远后，我把凉鞋那根「长度可调的带子」松了松。

examples.en: The adjustable strap on my top kept slipping down during the rehearsal.
examples.zh: 排练时，我上衣那根「长度可调的带子」老是滑下来。

collocations: an adjustable strap on a sandal

words.enDefinition: a set of clothes to put on in place of what you're wearing

examples.en: I packed a change of clothes for dinner after we finished working in the garden.
examples.zh: 我带了「一套换洗衣服」，在花园干完活后换好去吃晚饭。

examples.en: She keeps a change of clothes in her gym locker for the walk home.
examples.zh: 她在健身房储物柜里放了「一套换洗衣服」，换完可以走回家。

collocations: keep a change of clothes handy

words.enDefinition: a strand of sewing thread no longer held tightly in fabric

examples.en: I spotted a loose thread at my cuff just before I left for class.
examples.zh: 我刚要出门上课，就发现袖口有个「松脱的线头」。

examples.en: The loose thread on my jacket kept getting caught in the zipper that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，我夹克上的「松脱的线头」老是被拉链夹住。

collocations: a loose thread at the seam

words.enDefinition: a brush used to smooth or arrange hair

examples.en: I keep a hairbrush next to the mirror so I can get ready quickly.
examples.zh: 我把「发刷」放在镜子旁边，这样出门前能快点收拾好。

examples.en: My roommate found my hairbrush on the shelf beside our shared bathroom door.
examples.zh: 室友在共用浴室门边的架子上找到了我的「发刷」。

collocations: keep a hairbrush in your bag

words.enDefinition: a toothed tool used to arrange or smooth hair

examples.en: I packed a comb so I could tidy my hair after walking in the wind.
examples.zh: 我带了把「梳子」，走过风大的路段后可以整理一下头发。

examples.en: The comb was at the bottom of my bag under two notebooks and a towel.
examples.zh: 「梳子」在我包底，上面压着两本笔记本和一条毛巾。

collocations: run a comb through your hair

words.enDefinition: a comb with teeth spaced far apart

examples.en: I used a wide-tooth comb after swimming because my hair had tangled during practice.
examples.zh: 游泳训练时头发打了结，我游完用了一把「宽齿梳」。

examples.en: She took a wide-tooth comb from her bag while we waited for the bus.
examples.zh: 我们等公交时，她从包里拿出了一把「宽齿梳」。

words.enDefinition: an elastic band used to hold hair in place

examples.en: I found a hair tie on my wrist just before the pottery class started.
examples.zh: 陶艺课刚要开始，我发现手腕上正好有一根「束发皮筋」。

examples.en: She offered me a spare hair tie when I left mine in my room.
examples.zh: 我把自己的落在房间里了，她借了我一根备用的「束发皮筋」。

words.enDefinition: a small clasp used to hold a section of hair

examples.en: A hair clip kept my hair out of my face during the drawing session.
examples.zh: 上绘画课时，我用「发夹」把头发夹住，免得挡脸。

examples.en: My hair clip fell onto the desk when I leaned over my notebook.
examples.zh: 我俯身看笔记本时，「发夹」掉到了桌上。

words.enDefinition: a narrow flat pin used to hold a small section of hair

examples.en: I used a bobby pin to hold a loose strand before rehearsal started.
examples.zh: 排练开始前，我用一个「一字发夹」别住了散下来的一绺头发。

examples.en: We found a bobby pin on the dressing room shelf after the student concert.
examples.zh: 学生音乐会结束后，我们在更衣室的架子上找到一个「一字发夹」。

collocations: secure hair with a bobby pin

words.enDefinition: a band worn around the head to hold hair back

examples.en: I wore a headband to keep my hair out of my eyes during practice.
examples.zh: 训练时我戴了条「发带」，免得头发挡住眼睛。

examples.en: The headband stayed in my bag until I needed it for the group photo.
examples.zh: 「发带」一直在我包里，直到拍合照时我才拿出来用。

words.enDefinition: a line dividing the hair down the center of the head

examples.en: I made a middle part before tying my hair back for the workshop.
examples.zh: 去工坊前，我先分出一条「中分发缝」，再把头发扎起来。

examples.en: She moved the hair clip slightly to keep her middle part in place.
examples.zh: 她把发夹稍稍移了一下，好让「中分发缝」保持原位。

collocations: wear your hair with a middle part

words.enDefinition: a line dividing the hair to one side of the head

examples.en: I made a side part this morning before leaving for the campus theatre rehearsal.
examples.zh: 今天早上出门去学校剧院排练前，我给头发分了条「偏分发缝」。

examples.en: My side part shifted when I took off the hat outside the library.
examples.zh: 在图书馆外摘下帽子时，我的「偏分发缝」已经被压乱了。

collocations: wear your hair with a side part

words.enDefinition: hair cut so that it falls over the forehead

examples.en: I clipped my bangs back before leaning over the desk to finish the poster.
examples.zh: 我把「刘海」夹到后面，才俯身在桌上把海报画完。

examples.en: Her bangs slipped out from under her hat on the walk to class.
examples.zh: 去上课的路上，她的「刘海」从帽子下面露了出来。

collocations: wear your bangs to one side

words.enDefinition: hair gathered and tied at the back of the head

examples.en: I wore my hair in a ponytail so it stayed out of the clay.
examples.zh: 我把头发扎成「马尾辫」，这样就不会碰到黏土。

examples.en: My ponytail flattened against the back of my coat as I leaned against the wall.
examples.zh: 我往墙上一靠，「马尾辫」就压在外套后背上了。

collocations: tie your hair in a ponytail

words.enDefinition: hair twisted into a knot low on the back of the head

examples.en: I put my hair in a low bun before the college orchestra concert.
examples.zh: 学院管弦乐团音乐会开始前，我把头发盘成了「低盘发髻」。

examples.en: Her low bun fit easily under the hood of her raincoat on the way home.
examples.zh: 回家的路上，她雨衣的帽子能轻松罩住那个「低盘发髻」。

collocations: put your hair in a low bun

words.enDefinition: a length of hair woven together from several strands

examples.en: She wore her hair in a braid for the walk along the windy beach.
examples.zh: 沿着风大的海滩散步时，她把头发编成了「辫子」。

examples.en: I tied the end of my braid just before leaving the dorm for class.
examples.zh: 我在离开宿舍去上课前，把「辫子」的末端扎好。

collocations: tie the end of a braid

words.enDefinition: an occasion when your hair is cut or styled

examples.en: I booked a haircut for Saturday because my final project was due on Friday.
examples.zh: 毕业项目周五要交，所以我约了周六「理发」。

examples.en: The haircut took less time than I expected, and I still caught the bus.
examples.zh: 这次「理发」比我预计的快，我还赶上了公交。

words.enDefinition: a small cut to tidy hair or shorten it slightly

examples.en: I only asked for a trim before the choir's group photo on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五合唱团拍合影前，我只要求「稍微修剪一下头发」。

examples.en: The trim took about fifteen minutes, so I had time to walk across campus.
examples.zh: 这次「修剪头发」用了大概十五分钟，我还有时间走到校园另一头。

words.enDefinition: remove knots from hair so it can be combed freely

examples.en: I stopped to detangle my hair after taking off my scarf in the hallway.
examples.zh: 我在走廊摘下围巾后，停下来「梳开打结的头发」。

examples.en: It took me a minute to detangle my hair before the group photo.
examples.zh: 拍合影前，我花了一会儿「梳开打结的头发」。

words.enDefinition: dry hair using a hair dryer

examples.en: I had time to blow-dry my hair before meeting my roommate downstairs for dinner.
examples.zh: 下楼和室友碰面吃饭前，我还来得及「用吹风机吹干」头发。

examples.en: She prefers to blow-dry her hair before heading out to the bus stop.
examples.zh: 她喜欢「用吹风机吹干」头发，再出门去公交站。

collocations: get ready to blow-dry your hair

words.enDefinition: dry something by rubbing or pressing it with a towel

examples.en: I usually towel-dry my hair before grabbing my bag and leaving the shared bathroom.
examples.zh: 我通常先「用毛巾擦干」头发，再拎包离开共用浴室。

examples.en: She had time to towel-dry her hair before walking back from the campus pool.
examples.zh: 从学校游泳池走回去之前，她还来得及「用毛巾擦干」头发。

words.enDefinition: remove something from hair or fabric by washing it away with water

examples.en: I stayed in the shower a bit longer to rinse out the rest of the shampoo.
examples.zh: 我在淋浴间多待了一会儿，把剩余的洗发水「冲洗掉」。

examples.en: I had to rinse out the conditioner before turning off the water in the shower.
examples.zh: 关淋浴的水之前，我得把护发素「冲洗掉」。

words.enDefinition: make soap or shampoo form a mass of small bubbles

examples.en: I could lather the soap easily in the shower downstairs that morning.
examples.zh: 那天早上在楼下洗澡时，我很容易把肥皂「揉出泡沫」。

examples.en: It was easier to lather the soap once I had wet my hands.
examples.zh: 手沾湿以后，更容易把肥皂「揉出泡沫」。

words.enDefinition: a product used to clean the skin on your face

examples.en: I packed a small tube of face wash for the weekend trip with my flatmates.
examples.zh: 我带了一小管「洁面产品」，准备周末和室友一起出门玩。

examples.en: The face wash was still on the bathroom shelf when I got back from class.
examples.zh: 我下课回来时，「洁面产品」还在浴室架子上。

words.enDefinition: a product used to help keep skin from feeling dry

examples.en: I left my moisturizer on the shelf beside the mirror in the shared bathroom.
examples.zh: 我把「保湿护肤品」落在共用浴室镜子边的架子上了。

examples.en: My roommate packed a small tube of moisturizer for our weekend away from campus.
examples.zh: 我们周末要离开学校，室友带了一小管「保湿护肤品」。

words.enDefinition: soap made in a solid block rather than liquid form

examples.en: I put the bar soap on a plate while the bathroom shelf was being fixed.
examples.zh: 浴室架子还在修，我先把「块状肥皂」放在盘子上。

examples.en: We took bar soap on the trip because the cabin only had a small sink.
examples.zh: 小木屋只有一个小洗手池，所以我们出门带了「块状肥皂」。

words.enDefinition: a small container that holds a bar of soap

examples.en: I set the soap dish beside the sink so it wouldn't get knocked over.
examples.zh: 我把「肥皂托」放在洗手池旁边，这样不容易被碰翻。

examples.en: My roommate moved the soap dish to make space for another toothbrush cup.
examples.zh: 室友挪开「肥皂托」，腾地方放另一个牙刷杯。

collocations: put soap in the soap dish

words.enDefinition: a container for carrying or holding things used in the shower

examples.en: I carry my shower caddy down the hall when I use the shared bathroom.
examples.zh: 用共用浴室时，我会提着「淋浴用品篮」走过走廊。

examples.en: The shower caddy fits under my desk when I'm not using the shared showers.
examples.zh: 不用共用淋浴间时，「淋浴用品篮」正好可以收在我书桌下面。

words.enDefinition: a waterproof cap that keeps hair dry in the shower

examples.en: I wore a shower cap because I had already washed my hair after practice.
examples.zh: 我训练后已经洗过头，所以洗澡时戴了「浴帽」。

examples.en: She hung the shower cap beside her towel before heading back to her room.
examples.zh: 回房间前，她把「浴帽」挂在毛巾旁边。

words.enDefinition: a soft product applied to the skin before shaving

examples.en: I took a tube of shaving cream down the hall to the shared bathroom.
examples.zh: 我拿着一管「剃须膏」穿过走廊，去了共用浴室。

examples.en: The shaving cream was in my wash bag beside the toothbrush and comb.
examples.zh: 「剃须膏」在我的洗漱包里，放在牙刷和梳子旁边。

words.enDefinition: a small tool used to smooth or shape the edge of a nail

examples.en: I used a nail file after a rough edge kept catching on my sweater.
examples.zh: 指甲的毛边老是勾到毛衣，我就用了一下「指甲锉」。

examples.en: The nail file slipped behind the mirror when I set it on the shelf.
examples.zh: 我刚把「指甲锉」放到架子上，它就滑到镜子后面了。

words.enDefinition: a small tool with two arms used to pick up tiny objects

examples.en: I used tweezers to get a small thread out of the clasp on my hair clip.
examples.zh: 我用「小镊子」把卡在发夹搭扣里的一根细线夹了出来。

examples.en: My tweezers were at the bottom of the bag underneath the towel I'd packed.
examples.zh: 我的「小镊子」在包底，上面压着我带的毛巾。

collocations: keep tweezers in a wash bag

words.enDefinition: a small stick with a soft cotton tip

examples.en: I used a cotton swab to clear dust from the hinge of my hair clip.
examples.zh: 我用一根「棉签」清掉发夹转轴上的灰。

examples.en: A cotton swab rolled under the sink when I opened my wash bag.
examples.zh: 我打开洗漱包时，一根「棉签」滚到了洗手池下面。

words.enDefinition: a small square cloth used for washing your face or body

examples.en: I hung my washcloth beside the sink so it would dry before the morning.
examples.zh: 我把「洗脸小毛巾」挂在洗手池旁边，好让它第二天早上前晾干。

examples.en: The washcloth was still damp, so I left it out while I went to class.
examples.zh: 「洗脸小毛巾」还是潮的，我就把它晾在外面，自己去上课。
